subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm designing a compact cyberpunk-style armored riot-control vehicle with a water cannon turret, wheel joints, and neon accents, planning out the builder structure and joint hierarchy before writing the TypeScript module.

Setting dimensions and colors — a dark navy/armor palette with magenta and cyan neon highlights, plus hazard-stripe decals and corporate branding via SVG textures and panel paint effects.

Writing chassis setup...

I'm extending the lower body length and adding a nose wedge, then placing a horizontal water tank cylinder on the rear deck with straps and a filler dome. I'm also planning a turret on the cab roof with yaw/pitch joints and a forward-facing barrel ending in a glowing cyan nozzle, connected by a hose.

Now I'm detailing exterior accents: glowing roof light bars, neon side strips, underglow, slit-eye headlights, a riot ram bumper with teeth, mesh-barred cage windows, door joints, mirrors, antenna, lights, exhaust, spotlights, and optional riot shield racks — aiming for around 150 parts using repeated loops. Then I'm structuring the four wheels with steering joints up front, building tread-block tires merged into few parts and rims with neon accents.

Working through wheel details like torus-shaped glowing rim rings, lug nuts, dark fender arch boxes, and axle rotation along the correct axis. Then I'm figuring out how to orient a "NOVA SEC" shield logo plane on each side so the text reads correctly from the viewer's perspective, accounting for mirroring so it isn't backwards on one side.

Now I'm setting up turret mechanics: yaw and pitch joints at specific positions, a barrel rod with a lathe nozzle tip, a glowing cyan disc accent, and a catmull-curve hose sweep connecting the tank to the turret base.

For the wheels, I'm adding steer joints on the front hub pivoting around the vertical axis and spin joints for rotation, with rear wheels using simpler spin-only joints parented to the chassis. For the tread, I'm merging small box geometries using BufferGeometryUtils, computing them in local space before positioning each block at the hub with spin-bone animation along the local x-axis.

I'm placing a glowing neon rocker strip along each side between the wheel wells, adding an underglow box beneath the chassis, and defining the body's base paint using a mottled countershading pattern over a dark hull color.

Now I'm adding a hazard stripe decal on the bumper with yellow-and-black warning stripes, then making sure the wheels sit flush at ground level before composing everything together into the final model.
